description:
This provenance anchor establishes “Jesus Christ” solely as a named position appearing in the 2015 New Human compiled double issue. It is minted retrospectively from the printed textual manifestation under the Armature protocol and is classified as a retrospectively canonized named position in the Sappho class.

The body’s most important rule is non-reduction. The New Human charter does not disclose whether a printed voice is a civil-name author, a heteronym, or another form of position. Accordingly, this node neither asserts nor denies a relation between the 2015 byline and any civil identity. It also asserts nothing about the historical, theological, scriptural, literary, or living entities that share the string “Jesus Christ.” The position is distinguished only by its section in the 2015 issue.

The manifestation is the issue’s closing section, whose final printed words are “AS IT / MUST BE.” The anchor describes the byline as “the most retrospectively canonized named position on record” but immediately limits that claim to the issue’s jurisdiction. Its triple-attribution discussion—attributed author, communities of transmission, and MANUS as present archival authority—is an archive-theoretical interpretation rather than a historical claim about Christian authorship.

This record requires especially strong disambiguation metadata because a generic entity resolver could otherwise merge a narrow journal byline with a major historical-religious referent.

**Jesus Christ — Provenance Anchor** is a Crimson Hexagonal Archive record for a named position printed in *New Human Compiled, Ed. 1* in 2015.

The anchor concerns only that journal byline and its textual section. It does not assert that the position is identical or non-identical with the historical or religious figure Jesus Christ, or with any other bearer of the name.

The civil-name relation is deliberately withheld under the New Human charter. The position is distinguished solely by its manifestation in the compiled issue, whose closing section ends “AS IT / MUST BE.”
